spec_id.description: Three-digit spec ID (kept v1 specs 003-011, new v2 specs 101+)

primary_focus.description: One-line statement of what this spec chiefly measures

id.description: '<spec_id>-C<nn>', unique within the file, numbered in file order

tier.description: core = task-completion basics; competent = the correct modern approach; expert = empirically calibrated so current frontier models pass only ~40-60%

weight.description: Relative importance; default 2, centerpiece signals up to 6. Tier does not imply weight.

requirement.description: A single verifiable statement about the submission, evaluable on ANY submission (never conditional on the model's chosen approach)

met_when.description: Concrete criteria for a 'met' verdict; must be checkable by reading code

partial_when.description: Optional concrete criteria for 'partial'. If absent, partial is reserved for genuinely borderline implementations.

anti_patterns.description: Common wrong approaches that mean 'missed' (may reference AP-nn from anti-patterns.md)

spec_refs.description: Spec requirement numbers/sections this checkpoint traces to, e.g. 'Requirement 8'
